K2SymbolsBrauer.summary: Nothing K-theoretic in this roadmap exists: neither library has a Steinberg group, K₂ of a ring, Milnor K-theory, Steinberg or Dennis–Stein symbols, tame symbols, Weil reciprocity, a Hilbert symbol or a local invariant map. Tau Ceti's algebraic K-theory stops at K₀. The substrate is well developed and should be consumed rather than rebuilt: type-A commutator relations for elementary matrices in GL_n(A) (Tau Ceti), group homology in all degrees (Mathlib), classification of extensions with abelian kernel by H² (Tau Ceti), DVR unit parts, and Tau Ceti's function-field places with residues, norm residues, divisor evaluation, disjoint-support moving, finite support of orders and the product formula, all built as the apparatus for Weil reciprocity. For T.7 there are the Kummer map with its kernel and a (1,1) cup product on continuous cohomology. Genuinely missing: the Steinberg group and its universal central extension, K₂ ≅ H₂(E(A)) and the homotopy comparison, Matsumoto, the tame symbol and localisation sequence, Bass–Tate and Milnor transfers, Weil reciprocity itself, the tame kernel and K₂(ℤ), K₂(F_q), K₂(ℚ), Dennis–Stein symbols, and the Galois-symbol, Tate, Hilbert-symbol and reciprocity comparisons.

targets.target: Steinberg group St_n(A) presented by generators x_ij(a) and the Steinberg relations, with distinct-index hypotheses explicit
targets.note: Neither library has a Steinberg group of a ring. Mathlib has no occurrence of 'Steinberg'. Every Tau Ceti 'Steinberg' declaration is a Frobenius or graph-twisted Steinberg endomorphism of a group of Lie type (CFSG files), the Steinberg representation of GL₂(F_q), or the quaternion Steinberg relation, as the layer itself warns. Mathlib's `PresentedGroup` could carry the presentation. Tau Ceti proves that the relations hold for transvections in GL_n(A) (`commutatorElement_transvectionUnit`), which is the map St_n(A) → GL_n(A) would need.

K3BlochGroups.summary: Nothing in this roadmap exists in either library: there are no Bloch or pre-Bloch groups, five-term relations, cross-ratios, dilogarithms, Suslin sequence or enhanced Tor, and no K₃ of any ring. The Steinberg group underlying V.1 is absent too, and Tau Ceti's algebraic K-theory stops at K₀. What exists is general infrastructure: Mathlib's group homology by the bar complex with explicit degree-3 chains and chain maps, the Tor functor, roots of unity, tensor and exterior powers over ℤ, spectral sequences, the doubly transitive action of GL on the projective line, and the invariants r₁ and r₂. Genuinely missing is all of V.1–V.6, from K₃(A) ≅ H₃(St(A), ℤ) through the Bloch-group conventions and Suslin's theorem to K₃(F_q), K₃(ℤ) ≅ ℤ/48 and K₃(ℚ(i)), Bloch-element certificates and the regulator comparisons.

KTheoryFiniteLocalFields.summary: Almost none of this roadmap exists. The one target already built beyond imports is K₀(F_q) = ℤ, which Tau Ceti proves for every division ring by dimension; the Witt-vector algebra L.5 consumes is complete in Mathlib. There is no K_n of a ring for n ≥ 1, no finite-coefficient K-theory, Bockstein sequence or rigidity, no topological K-theory or Bott periodicity, no Brauer lifting or Adams operations, no Hochschild, cyclic, THH, TR or TC, no de Rham–Witt complex, no Hilbert symbol or local Tate duality, and no Tate twists ℤ_p(j). The supporting arithmetic that exists should be consumed: henselian instances for local rings of integers and adic completions, the unit filtration and Teichmüller identification μ_{q−1} ≅ k^×, |GL_n(F_q)|, Frobenius and norms of finite fields, Kähler differentials, continuous cohomology and the cyclotomic character. Genuinely missing: Quillen's calculation, rigidity, Moore's theorem for K₂ of local fields, the trace calculations and all local higher K-group descriptions and local-to-global compatibilities.

KTheoryLowDegrees.summary: Tau Ceti already supplies the degree-zero foundation this roadmap plans to build on. It has K₀ of finitely generated projectives over any ring (`finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure`, proved split), with its universal property, the Cartan map to G₀ and the resolution theorem, and K₀ ≅ ℤ for division rings. It also has the type-A commutator relations and SL_n = E_n over fields and over ℤ. Mathlib supplies projectives as retracts of Rⁿ, the locally constant rank on Spec with base change, freeness over local rings, Pic with Cl ≃ Pic for domains, and rank-one Steinitz; Tau Ceti adds Cl(𝒪_S) ≅ Cl/⟨S⟩ and E(F) as the degree-zero divisor class group. Genuinely missing: GL(A), E(A) and K₁ with Whitehead's lemma, the determinant/SK₁ theory and Bass–Milnor–Serre, the S-unit rank formula, relative K₁ and transfers, λ-operations and det: K₀ → Pic, Steinitz in rank ≥ 2 and K₀ ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic, K₀ of schemes and curves, the projective-bundle formula, and every comparison with higher K-theory.

targets.target: GL(A) as the filtered colimit of the GL_n(A) along g ↦ diag(g,1), with finite representatives and equality after a common stabilisation
targets.note: Mathlib's `DirectLimit` carries a group structure for a directed system of groups, but neither library builds the stabilisation embedding GL_n(A) → GL_{n+1}(A) or the colimit of the tower.

targets.note: The elementary matrices exist in GL: Mathlib's `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.transvection` and Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.transvectionUnit` (any commutative ring). Block sums exist only as Tau Ceti's `LinearMap.GeneralLinearGroup.prodMap` on GL(V) × GL(W) → GL(V × W), with multiplicativity lemmas. The matrix block-sum homomorphism GL_m(A) × GL_n(A) → GL_{m+n}(A) is missing.

targets.target: The stable elementary subgroup E(A)
targets.note: No elementary subgroup E_n(A) of GL_n(A) is named for a general ring, and there is no stable version. Tau Ceti's `transvectionUnit_mem_of_adjacent` shows that a subgroup of GL_{m+1}(A) containing the adjacent transvections contains all of them. The elementary subgroups in Tau Ceti's Lie-theory files belong to Chevalley groups, not to GL_n of a ring.

targets.note: Tau Ceti proves these in GL_n(A) and in SL_n(A) over an arbitrary commutative ring, for distinct indices i, j, l: `TauCeti.commutatorElement_transvectionUnit`, with `commute_transvectionUnit` for the non-chaining pairs. These are the finite-rank identities with explicit index hypotheses that the layer asks for.

targets.note: Mathlib proves that SL(2,F) is perfect over a field with some a ≠ 0, a² ≠ 1 (`Matrix.SL2.commutator_eq_top`). Missing: perfectness of E_n(A) for n ≥ 3 over a ring, and of E(A).

targets.target: Test: diag(g, g⁻¹) has trivial class after stabilisation
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `diag2nUnit_decompose` proves the scalar case: diag(a, a⁻¹) for a unit a is a product of transvections, over any commutative ring. Missing: the block-matrix case diag(g, g⁻¹) for g ∈ GL_n(A), and the K₁ statement.

targets.target: Test: the valuation boundary of a uniformiser is 1
targets.note: Absent with the boundary map.

duplicates.note: Identifies the explicit K₁ model with the degree-one group of the K-theory space, the comparison this layer states as π₁BGL(A)⁺ ≅ GL(A)/E(A).
Its K_{2j−1}(F_q) ≅ ℤ/(q^j−1) at j = 1, with the recovery of the determinant in degree one, is this layer's K₁ of a finite field.
Computes the first four K-groups of ℤ, including this layer's K₁(ℤ).

targets.target: Finitely generated projectives are the direct summands of finite free modules, with the complement, splitting maps and idempotent available
targets.note: `Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective` exhibits a finitely generated projective as a retract of Rⁿ, with f ∘ g = id, and `Module.Projective.of_split` gives the converse. The idempotent endomorphism g ∘ f of Rⁿ, which is the idempotent matrix, and `LinearMap.isProj_iff_isIdempotentElem` relating idempotents to projections, are available.

targets.target: Correspondence between idempotent matrices up to stabilised equivalence and isomorphism classes of finitely generated projectives
targets.note: Mathlib matches idempotent endomorphisms with complemented submodules (`Submodule.isIdempotentElemEquiv`), but there is no classification of projectives by idempotent matrices up to stabilised conjugacy.

targets.target: Ring K₀ defined through the existing split/exact K₀ universal property
targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the exact category of finitely generated projective modules over any ring (`finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure`, in `Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/CartanMap.lean`). Its exact K₀ carries the universal property for additive invariants (`ExactK0.liftEquiv`); `SplitK0.liftEquiv` is the split version.

targets.target: Object-class induction and equality of classes by stable isomorphism
targets.note: Every element is a difference [P] − [Q] (`SplitK0.exists_eq_sub`). The comparison with Mathlib's group completion of the monoid of isomorphism classes (`SplitK0.grothendieckAddGroupEquiv`) and Schanuel's lemma are present. Missing: the statement that [P] = [Q] exactly when P ⊕ Rⁿ ≅ Q ⊕ Rⁿ for some n.

targets.target: Scalar extension and Morita functoriality of ring K₀
targets.note: The generic pieces exist: `SplitK0.map` and `mapEquiv` along additive functors and equivalences, base change preserving projectivity (`Module.Projective.tensorProduct`) and Mathlib's Morita equivalence, including R ~ Mₙ(R). Missing: the scalar-extension map on ring K₀ and Morita invariance of K₀.

targets.target: Direct-sum relations suffice, because every short exact sequence of projectives with projective quotient splits
targets.note: `finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure_eq_split` proves that the exact structure on finitely generated projectives is the split one, and `ExactK0.fromSplitEquiv` identifies split and exact K₀ in that situation. The underlying module fact is Mathlib's `LinearMap.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective`.

duplicates.note: Also constructs the exact category of finitely generated projectives with scalar extension, identifies π₀ with K₀(A), and proves that every finitely generated projective has a complement making it free.
Defines K₀(proj A) for a finite-dimensional algebra and proves its Morita invariance, the special case of this layer's Morita functoriality.

targets.target: Rank of a finitely generated projective over a commutative ring as a locally constant function on Spec A, constant on a connected spectrum
targets.note: `Module.rankAtStalk M : PrimeSpectrum R → ℕ` is locally constant for finitely presented flat modules (`isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`), which covers finitely generated projectives via `Module.Flat.of_projective`. On a connected spectrum it is constant by `IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace`. It is ℕ-valued, which is the stated integer rank.

targets.target: Finite image of the rank function and compatibility with localisation and base change
targets.note: Finite image: `IsLocallyConstant.range_finite` on the compact space Spec A. Base change is `Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange`, and more generally `rankAtStalk_isBaseChange`. Localisation is the base change along A → S⁻¹A (`LocalizedModule.isBaseChange`). Mathlib also has multiplicativity under tensor products.

targets.target: K₀(F) ≅ ℤ for fields and division rings, by dimension
targets.note: `TauCeti.SplitK0.finrankEquiv : SplitK0 (FGModuleCat k) ≃+ ℤ` for any division ring k, sending a class to its dimension, and the abelian version `AbelianK0.finrankEquiv`. It is stated on the category of finite-dimensional k-modules. Over a division ring this is the category of finitely generated projectives; the transport to `finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure k` goes through `SplitK0.mapEquiv`.

targets.target: Finite-product formula for K₀, and the test K₀(F × F) ≅ ℤ²
targets.note: No product formula for K₀ of rings. Only its rank shadow exists: `Module.rankAtStalk_prod` and `rankAtStalk_pi`.

targets.target: Finitely generated projectives over a local ring are free
targets.note: `Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing` shows that a finite flat module over a local ring is free. With `Module.Flat.of_projective` this is more general than the layer's Nakayama and finite-presentation route.

targets.target: The semilocal decomposition, stated with its connected-component information
targets.note: Mathlib proves that over a ring with finitely many maximal ideals, a finite flat module of constant rank at the maximal ideals is free (`Module.free_of_flat_of_finrank_eq`, Stacks 02M9). Missing: the decomposition of K₀ of a semilocal ring by connected components.

duplicates.note: States K₀(F_q) = ℤ, the finite-field case of this layer's K₀(F) ≅ ℤ for fields.

targets.target: The ring structure on K₀ of a commutative ring from the tensor product
targets.note: Tau Ceti gives `SplitK0 C` a commutative ring structure, with [X]·[Y] = [X ⊗ Y], for any braided monoidal preadditive category with biproducts (`SplitK0.instCommRing`). Missing: the monoidal structure on finitely generated projective modules that would give ring K₀ this multiplication.

targets.target: Exterior powers of finite projectives and the filtration formula for an extension
targets.note: Mathlib defines ⋀[R]^n M for every module, with freeness and the rank formula (n choose k) for free modules, and the exterior algebra of a product. Missing: projectivity of ⋀ⁿ of a finitely generated projective, and the filtration of ⋀ⁿ M for 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0.

targets.target: λ-ring identities on K₀, extended from modules to virtual classes
targets.note: There is no λ-ring, γ-operation or Adams operation in either library. `BinomialRing` exists, and Mathlib's docstrings (`Binomial.lean`, `Dickson.lean`) record that λ-rings are not formalised.

targets.target: The determinant of a projective of locally constant rank, defined componentwise, compared with Pic
targets.note: Only the free case exists: for a module with a basis of size n, Tau Ceti identifies ⋀ⁿM with R (`exteriorPower.topEquiv`) and shows endomorphisms act on it by det. Mathlib proves that a stably free invertible module is free. Missing: the top exterior power of a projective of locally constant rank as an invertible module.

targets.target: Determinant as an additive homomorphism K₀(A) → Pic(A), with tensor product as the Picard operation
targets.note: The target `CommRing.Pic`, the group of invertible modules under tensor product, exists; the determinant map on K₀ does not.

targets.target: The augmentation (rank) kernel and its relation with the γ-filtration; degree-zero normalisation of the Adams operations
targets.note: No γ-filtration and no Adams operations in either library.

duplicates.note: Compares the external product with tensor products on K₀, the same K₀ ring structure this layer constructs.
Constructs λ-operations and Adams operations on K-theory, whose degree-zero part is this layer's λ-ring structure on K₀.
Constructs the γ-filtration, which this layer relates to the rank kernel.

targets.target: Steinitz classification: a positive-rank finite projective over a Dedekind domain is free plus an invertible ideal
targets.note: Only rank one is present: Mathlib proves that every invertible module over a domain is isomorphic to an ideal (`Module.Invertible.exists_linearEquiv_ideal`). Missing: the decomposition in rank ≥ 2. Mathlib's Dedekind-domain module theory otherwise covers torsion modules and 'flat iff torsion-free'.

targets.target: I ⊕ J ≅ A ⊕ IJ for invertible ideals
targets.note: Not stated in either library.

targets.target: (rank, det): K₀(A) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(A) for a Dedekind domain, with its inverse, independence of ideal representatives, and the zero module separately
targets.note: Both components of the target exist (`CommRing.Pic`, `Module.rankAtStalk`), but neither the determinant map nor the isomorphism does.

targets.target: Comparison of Pic with the existing ideal class group
targets.note: `ClassGroup.equivPic : ClassGroup R ≃* Pic R` holds for every domain, which is more general than the Dedekind case.

targets.target: Specialisation to O_F and O_{F,S}: the class group of the S-integers is the class group modulo the classes of the primes in S
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Cl(𝒪_S) ≃* Cl(R)/⟨[v] : v ∈ S⟩ for any Dedekind domain R (`IsDedekindDomain.integerClassGroupEquiv`). There 𝒪_S is the valuation-defined overring `Set.integer`, which its docstring notes is not in general a localisation. Missing: the K₀ statement, and the identification with the localised ring the layer names.

targets.target: Induced maps under localisation, extension of number fields and finite flat restriction of scalars; transfer of an ideal class by the determinant/norm formula
targets.note: The Pic-level maps exist: extension of ideal classes (`ClassGroup.extendedHom`) and the relative norm on class groups, with norm ∘ extension = [L:K]-th power (`ClassGroup.relNorm`, `relNorm_extendedHom`). Missing: the maps on K₀ and the transfer's determinant formula.

targets.target: K₀ of finite locally free sheaves on a scheme, from the categorical construction
targets.note: `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree` exists, but no exact category of vector bundles and no K₀ of a scheme.

targets.target: K₀(X) ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic(X) by rank and determinant, for a connected regular noetherian curve
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti's `LineBundleClass X` is only a commutative monoid of isomorphism classes of invertible sheaves, with inverses deliberately not provided, so there is no Pic(X) group to map to.

targets.target: Structure-sheaf and skyscraper-sheaf class formulas through the K/G comparison, so that a divisor class agrees with a line-bundle class
targets.note: Tau Ceti maps Weil divisor classes to line-bundle classes additively and injectively on integral noetherian schemes of dimension ≤ 1 whose codimension-one local rings are DVRs (`classGroupToLineBundleClass_injective`, `classGroupToLineBundleClassHom`). Surjectivity is not proved. The K-theoretic class formulas need K₀ and G₀ of the curve, which are missing.

targets.target: Pic(E) ≅ ℤ ⊕ E(F) for an elliptic curve with rational origin, hence K₀(E) ≅ ℤ² ⊕ E(F); not for genus-one curves without a rational point
targets.note: Tau Ceti has both halves at the level of function-field divisor classes. E(F) is the degree-zero class group (`pointEquivDegreeZeroDivisorClass`, via `Point.toClassEquiv`), and a class group with a degree-one point splits as Pic⁰ × ℤ (`OrderSystem.classGroupAddEquivPicZeroProdInt`; `ker_degreeClass_eq_picZero` identifies the function-field Pic⁰). Missing: the scheme-level Picard group of E and the K₀ consequence.

duplicates.note: Also proves the Picard decomposition Pic(E) ≅ ℤ ⊕ E(F) on an elliptic curve with rational origin and K₀(E) ≅ ℤ² ⊕ E(F).
Owns the Weil/Cartier/line-bundle dictionary Cl(X) ≅ Pic X on a smooth curve and its degree, the divisor-class/line-bundle agreement this layer uses.

targets.target: Agreement of these definitions and maps with π₀ of the general K-theory
targets.note: No higher K-theory space or spectrum exists in either library, so there is no π₀K to compare with.

targets.target: Localisation sends a projective class to its localised class and a perfect complex to its Euler class
targets.note: No K₀ localisation map and no perfect complexes of modules. Tau Ceti's Euler class of bounded complexes in abelian K₀ (`AbelianK0.eulerChar`) is the nearest construction.

targets.target: Comparison of the Cartan map K₀ → G₀ with the existing general Cartan map
targets.note: The existing general Cartan map is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.cartanMap : K₀(proj R) →+ G₀(mod R)` for any ring. It is an isomorphism when every finitely generated module has a finite projective resolution (`cartanEquiv`). Any ring K₀ built on `finiteProjectiveModulesExactStructure` uses it directly. Missing: the scheme-level Cartan map and the comparison of the layer's degree-zero maps with it.

targets.target: Tests: fields, ℤ, a product of two fields, and a Dedekind domain with a nonprincipal ideal class
targets.note: K₀ of a field or division ring is computed (`SplitK0.finrankEquiv`). Missing: K₀(ℤ), K₀(F × F), and the nonprincipal-ideal test, which needs K₀ ≅ ℤ ⊕ Pic.

targets.target: K₀(P¹_F) ≅ ℤ² by the projective-bundle construction and by rank/Pic, with the two bases compared
targets.note: No projective-bundle formula and no K₀ of a scheme in either library.

duplicates.note: Identifies the components of the K-theory space of A with K₀(A): the same agreement of ring K₀ with π₀K.
Proves the projective-bundle theorem and compares it with this layer's P¹ calculation, i.e. K₀(P¹_F) ≅ ℤ².
Computes the K-theory of P¹ by the projective-bundle theorem, including this layer's K₀(P¹_F) ≅ ℤ² test.
Computes the first four K-groups of ℤ, including this layer's K₀(ℤ) test.
